target.notes: Byte-identical to the live master's running /usr/sbin/soapc

cross_version_target.openssl_imports_delta: none (every OpenSSL JUMP_SLOT symbol identical to 7215)

notes_on_openssl_defaults: OpenSSL 1.1.1: SSL_CTX_new() initialises verify_mode to SSL_VERIFY_NONE. SSL_CTX_set_options(ctx, 0) is a no-op (OR 0 into existing options). Without a subsequent SSL_CTX_set_verify / SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations / SSL_CTX_set_cert_store call, the client accepts ANY server certificate — self-signed, wrong-hostname, expired. This is the documented OpenSSL default behaviour.

libcurl.so.4.comment: libcurl is NOT referenced by soapc so curl_easy_setopt(CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER) cannot be a hidden mechanism

call_sequence_in_order.note: OpenSSL initialisation, not a verify call
Second argument is the literal constant 0. OR-ing 0 into the options mask is a no-op. This call configures NOTHING.

call_sequence_in_order.post_handshake_actions: if return==1 log success; else log failure. In BOTH branches control falls through to SSL_write/SSL_read loop. NO SSL_get_verify_result/SSL_get_peer_certificate/X509_* call anywhere after SSL_connect.

tls_pipeline_in_soapc_sendRequest.ca_bundle_path_strings_in_soapc: none — binary contains zero occurrences of /etc/ssl, cacert, ca-bundle, ca.pem, certs.pem, etc.
tls_pipeline_in_soapc_sendRequest.hostname_validation_implementation: none — neither X509_check_host nor manual CN extraction nor getnameinfo-based comparison present. The host string param_2 is used only in logging (fprintf of the connect-target).

host_param_data_flow: param_2 (satellite host string) is read from NVRAM key soapc_sat_<idx>_ip (confirmed in report 33 and via inspection of soapc_sendRequest prologue). It is passed to FUN_00022e88 (TCP-connect helper) which performs getaddrinfo + connect(2). It is ALSO passed to the fprintf-log calls after SSL_connect. It is NOT passed to any X509 or hostname-comparison API because no such API is imported.
sat_side_server_posture_note: sat lighttpd serves /soap/server_sa over :443. Its server cert is a self-signed device cert (per report 31's TLS inspection at fingerprint 4688...1a2b). A VERIFY_NONE client accepts this cert and ANY substitute cert without warning.
method_classification: left_disabled_by_default_in_SSL_CTX_new (OpenSSL 1.1.1 SSL_VERIFY_NONE default; no explicit SSL_CTX_set_verify call to raise or lower). The one call that SOUNDS like it could configure security (SSL_CTX_set_options with arg=0) is a no-op.
report33_claim_status: UPHELD — report 33's conclusion (no certificate verification) is correct. The nuance added here: the correct precise statement is NOT 'explicitly disabled' but 'left at the OpenSSL default SSL_VERIFY_NONE because no verify-mode call was ever made'. The security impact is identical. soapc accepts any certificate the satellite presents.
